messages:
Priya S: Quick note 17:30 UTC today were putting a release freeze on the v3.6 train. No merges except approved exceptions.
Priya S: Canary scheduled for 08:00 UTC tomorrow, 90m window, canary-a then canary-b.
Priya S: Minimal checklist:
```
- freeze branches (no non-critical merges)
- tag: rc/v3.6.0
- upload artifacts to artifact-repo
- run canary smoke suite on canary-a
- watch p95/p99, error-rate, and memory pressure
- rollback plan prepared (v3.5 fallback)
```
Owen M: Heads-up from staging: streaming-runtime showed a transient heap growth during long-tail requests after the stress test. I have a tiny cap/fix that trims buffer sizes. Not customer-facing but reduces p99 by ~120ms.
Priya S: Let's not change behavior mid-canary unless it's a regression fix. Can you open a freeze-exception and tag release-shadow?
Owen M: done. @release-shadow PTAL, exception request: include streaming-runtime buffer trim in canary-b only to validate tail-latency improvement. Reason: reduce p99 and guard mem pressure.
release-shadow: Reviewed. Approve limited exception for canary-b only, must be toggleable and have immediate rollback steps. Marking accepted.
infra-bot: Pre-canary health: cluster CPU 64% used, mem pressure low, node restarts 0 in last 24h.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled at 08:00 UTC to canary-a then canary-b. Notifications: enabled.
Priya S: Rotation: Priya S, Maria G, Owen M. Escalation: @sre. Keep updates short.
deploy-bot: Canary started 08:00:00 UTC -> canary-a.
infra-bot: Canary-a health +10m: p95=140ms, error-rate=0.01%, mem pressure nominal.
Priya S: moving to canary-b with buffer-trim change scoped to canary-b only. Will monitor closely.
deploy-bot: Deploy to canary-b started 08:25:00 UTC.
infra-bot: Canary-b +15m: p95 increased to 520ms, p99 1.2s, error-rate 0.6%. Alerting owners.
Owen M: Investigating logs, seeing repeated GC stalls in canary-b after the change. Might be an interaction with the allocator on that pool.
Priya S: Pause further rollouts. Rollback change on canary-b now.
deploy-bot: Rolling back canary-b change to previous artifact (rc/v3.6.0 - streaming-runtime prior).
infra-bot: Canary-b post-rollback +5m: p95 back to 150ms, p99 320ms, error-rate 0.02%. GC stalls no longer observed.
Owen M: Thanks. I'll instrument a more conservative patch and run it in staging; we won't reintroduce it in this train. Opening a follow-up ticket: INF-1245.
Maria G: Good catch. Because of the rollback well extend canary window by 30m to validate system stability, then decide on promoting.
deploy-bot: Canary extended by 30m; new window end: 09:45 UTC.
infra-bot: System health throughout extension: stable. p95 avg 145ms, errors <0.05%.
Priya S: Decision: promote rc/v3.6.0 (without the buffer-trim) to gradual rollout after 09:45 UTC if no regressions. Release embargo will lift 1.5h after successful promote.
Owen M: Filing a postmortem-style note in INF, will include profiling data and allocator trace.
Maria G: Thanks team. If anyone needs an exception for the next train, open early. Final: keep notifications tight, only call out major regressions.
infra-bot: Reminder: automated incident will post to #incidents if error-rate >1% sustained for 5m or p99 >1s.
deploy-bot: Canary window closed 09:46:15 UTC. No further anomalies.
Priya S: All set 1:00 UTC we'll publish the release candidate readiness summary to exec and product. Short summary: canary passed after one rollback, no customer impact.
Maria G: :thumbsup:
